text:
micah: Heads-up — saw 3 OOMs on kv-cache-prod between 01:20 and 03:40 UTC. All on shard-14. Heap growth looks like steady KV fragmenting + occasional large transient allocs. Adding the short pprof snapshot below.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0452 (kv-cache OOM on shard-14) — paging eng-runtime oncall.

micah: pprof summary (top allocations):
```
1. 42%   runtime.mallocgc
2. 18%   github.com/redwood/kv.(*Shard).InsertLarge
3. 12%   bytes.MakeSlice
4. 8%    github.com/redwood/kv/cache.(*KVCache).Get
```
Heap grows with insert bursts, GC doesn't compact fragments quickly.

lena: Thanks for the dump. Do we have a recent change to shard size heuristics or the compaction threshold?

micah: No infra change in the last 7 days. There was a change in InsertLarge logic in commit 62d3a7 (attempt to batch writes) but it landed two weeks ago. Pattern suggests long-lived small fragments + a few huge allocations from InsertLarge.

jorge: I'll take ownership of profiling/patching InsertLarge. Plan: reproduce on a dev shard, add allocation annotations, try rolling back the batching in a canary. ETA: end of day Friday for initial repro and a hypothesis.

adarsh: I'll own fragmentation/GC tuning. I want to test lowering GC trigger threshold on a dedicated canary and enable more aggressive compaction. Also will add a heap-snapshot cron to catch growth early. ETA: Monday 9am for test results.

sarah: I'll own ops mitigations: put an emergency rate-limit on large Put requests for the next 48h and add an automatic shard-fallback to spare capacity. I'll open the PR and the rollout plan. ETA: 2 hours.

lena: Action list so far:
- jorge: reproduce & patch InsertLarge (EOD Fri)
- adarsh: GC tuning + snapshot cron (Mon 09:00)
- sarah: ops mitigations + PR (in 2h)
- micah: collect two more pprof dumps during next window and attach to INC-2026-0452

micah: noted — will attach the additional dumps. Also suggesting a postmortem entry for recurring pattern (kv-cache frag) and a follow-up on long-term: consider refactor of allocation path or streaming writes to avoid big temp buffers.

jorge: Quick note: before patching I want to run the microbenchmark for InsertLarge with and without the batching logic; if rollback shows improvement I'll draft a canary rollout (shard-by-shard) and a mitigation flag.

adarsh: If compaction reduces tail latency we should measure CPU cost. I'll create a dashboard for compaction-related CPU vs fragmentation over time.

sarah: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/ops/PR-719 — implements request-size rate-limiter and emergency fallback. Marked for fast-track.

lena: Good. Let's do a check-in tomorrow 10am UTC. Please update the incident ticket with owners + links to PRs and reproducer steps. Also add a recurring weekly check for kv-cache frag regressions.

micah: Will update INC-2026-0452 with pprofs and the reproducer. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: Incident review in 24h for INC-2026-0452

jorge: logging note — when reproducing, run with `KV_DEBUG_ALLOC=1 ./kv-run --shard=14` to get allocation histogram. Saves a lot of time.

adarsh: Added task to tracker: KVR-231 (weekly frag regression dashboard).

sarah: Ops mitigation deployed to canary in the last 30m. Canary showed 0 OOMs during the 1h test. Rolling to 25% now.

lena: Thanks. If the canary holds, schedule a full roll by Monday morning but coordinate with adarsh for compaction changes to avoid overlapping risky deploys.

micah: Copy. We'll keep status updates in the incident thread.

sarah: FYI, created slack alert channel #kv-oom-alerts for oncall paging and early telemetry.

lena: Closing loop: assign postmortem owner after incident stable. Propose micah or jorge — decide in 24h.
